## Metadata

- Report ID: IR-2026-1010
- Change reference: run-5f4422f26c3e / fix-bug / verify-validators-v4-instance-selection, implementing the Fix Strategy and Validation Plan of the root-cause analysis (BA-run-5f4422f26c3e-root-cause-analysis, digest sha256:e3a5f2bd434c91ec13e2debc49c0b829); the triage analysis (digest sha256:cb26b654658d79427e40bd8774105538) is supporting context
- Workflow phase: fix-implementation
- Status: complete
- Verification status: verified
- Review status: pending-review

## Implementation Summary

- Change intent: check V4 of the validator coverage verifier no longer depends on which run sorts last or on identifier rendering: the orchestration mutation finds its Phase Progression row by an identifier cell with or without backticks, and each type's instance is the first candidate on which the declared mutation resolves, with every skipped candidate reported and a loud V4 failure naming every candidate when none applies; V3 validates exactly the instance V4 mutates; the console mutation line prints the observed outcome. On unchanged run evidence the verifier reports 6/6 COVERED, with the run-d8937789961e closure record selected, caught by O4 alone, and no candidate skipped.
- Approach taken: in runtime/verify_validators.py, `award_itself_its_own_gate` matches column one against a new `PHASE_ID_CELL` pattern (optional backticks, the rule of the contract engine's defined_ids) instead of requiring a backticked identifier anywhere on the line; a new `candidate_instances` beside committed_instances lists committed instances last to first in the existing lexical run-identifier order, then governance records last to first, then the fixture; `conforming_instance` walks that list and returns `(instance, source, envelope, skipped)`, skipping a candidate only when `resolve_mutation` finds no anchor, never consulting validator acceptance or the mutation verdict; a small `instance_label` gives the printed path; the V3/V4 loop in main unpacks the four values, records each skip in the V4 detail (passing or failing), the console, and the JSON summary, and when no candidate applies fails V4 naming each candidate while V3 still validates the first candidate tried; a new `mutation_outcome` renders the console line from the finding. Rungs of the ladder: the new functions are rung 7 (the analysis names the candidate helper; no existing function lists candidates, labels a path, or renders an outcome); no file and no dependency was added. The first repair's recommend_an_unevaluated_option, resolve_mutation and mutation_verdict are unchanged. The test module gained ten tests; the bundled mirror was regenerated by its sync command.
- Design reference: root-cause analysis Fix Strategy (rendering-neutral row locator; fixed candidate order taking the first on which the mutation resolves; no filtering on validator acceptance; skipped candidates always reported; loud failure naming every candidate; docstring stops calling the order newest; console line reports the observed outcome; no validator, template, fixture or run evidence change) and its Validation Plan (reproduction expecting 6/6, the listed regression tests, full suite).
- Out of scope: every validator, template, fixture and committed run artifact; the orchestration contract's identifier rendering, routed by the analysis to architect; the F7 rejection of the change proposal from inside the framework directory, a separate defect the analysis routes to omn-tech-lead; candidate order by creation time, rejected by the analysis; the count-based derivations, which the new fallback now covers; observing the main checkout and hosted CI, routed to omn-qa.

## Deviations and Tradeoffs

| ID | Deviation | Design element | Rationale | Escalation |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `V-001` | When no candidate carries the mutation, the loop in `C-001` fails V4 naming every candidate and still runs V3 on the first candidate tried | Fix Strategy: V4 fails naming every candidate; V3 validates the instance V4 uses | V4 uses no instance in that case, and skipping V3 for the type would let a rejection go unreported; validating the first candidate keeps V3 exactly as strict as before the change | not-required |
| `V-002` | The full suite was not run before the first edit to `C-001` and `C-002`; the pre-change reference is the module-level baseline of the verifier and its test module | Reasoning Stage 2: execute the covering suite before changing anything | The covering suite for the impacted module is the verifier itself and its test module, both run first; the post-change full suite passed every module, so no failure needed attribution | not-required |
| `V-003` | Four of the new tests in `C-002` fail on the pre-fix verifier by the missing function or four-value return shape rather than by assertion, and the locator guard test passes on both | Validation Plan: each test fails before the fix and passes after | Those tests pin the new contract (fallback to the fixture, none naming every candidate, a non-conforming candidate kept, outcome text); the pre-fix selector had no such contract to assert against, and the guard pins that the wider locator still finds no row without a gated orchestrator row | not-required |
| `V-004` | The existing every-row sweep in `C-002` now unpacks four values from the selector | Fix Strategy regression scope: the existing test unpacks the selector's result | The return shape changed by design; the sweep's assertions are unchanged | not-required |

## Boundary Compliance

- Module boundaries preserved: the verifier still only reads run evidence, governance records, fixtures and registries and writes mutated copies to a temporary directory; no validator, template, fixture or committed run artifact changed; selection consults only resolve_mutation, never a validator or the mutation verdict; the tests build every candidate in a temporary directory and patch the selector's inputs in memory.
- Public interface changes: conforming_instance now returns four values `(instance, source, envelope, skipped)`; new module functions candidate_instances, instance_label and mutation_outcome and the PHASE_ID_CELL pattern; the JSON summaries gain `skipped_candidates` and `mutation.finding`, with the schema name validator-coverage.v1 unchanged; the V4 detail gains a skipped-candidates clause; the command line is unchanged.
- Data or migration impact: none; no store, schema or run evidence format changed
- Declared side effects: the three Change Set files, plus this artifact at runs/run-5f4422f26c3e/states/fix-implementation/artifacts/implementation-report.md and the result envelope at runs/run-5f4422f26c3e/states/fix-implementation/result-envelope.json. The suite run appended replay records to the committed run run-c5a8d50d3238, restored with `git checkout --`; no file under run-437e2f765e4b, run-d8937789961e or run-5f4422f26c3e changed during this phase apart from the two outputs. The pre-fix copy, harness and JSON report lie in the scratch directory outside the repository.

repositoryWrites.scopePhasesRationale: This grant is automated test files only, and only in the `safety-net-establishment` phase of refactor, where establishing the safety net is the phase's declared output. Production source is never written in any phase, and this grant does not apply outside the one phase named above.
repositoryWrites.rationale: QA judges behavior, not code, so it does not author the change it validates. One phase is the exception the framework declares deliberately: a refactor cannot be validated at all until a safety net exists, and building that net is the phase's whole purpose. Even there the boundary holds, because a test that pins existing behavior is not the change under validation. Every other phase reads the repository and writes only its own artifact and result envelope.
